question: Let $R$ be a relation on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined by $a R b$ if and only if $a - b$ is a multiple of $7$. Let $[3]$ denote the equivalence class of $3$ under $R$. Which of the following sets is $[3]$?
explanation:
The equivalence class of $3$ consists of all integers $b$ such that $b - 3$ is a multiple of $7$, i.e., $b \equiv 3 \pmod{7}$.

Option B: $\{x \in \mathbb{Z} \mid x \equiv 3 \pmod{7}\}$ is correct (since the equivalence class contains all such $x$ — both positive and negative values congruent to $3$ mod $7$).
